target_note: Asset-side baseline: Blender 5.2.1; documentation baseline: Blender 5.2 LTS Manual. Engine examples are version-stated documentation reads, not a production engine target and not runtime verification.

sources.title: Armature Skinning Introduction and Armature Deform Parenting
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Parenting versus deformation; Armature Deform parenting creates/sets up an Armature modifier
supports: Bone/object parenting moves children but does not deform their vertices
Armature Modifier plus weights is the deforming mechanism
Armature Deform parenting is a shortcut that adds an Armature modifier
limits: No game-engine consumption guarantee
Object parenting plus modifier is not automatically a double transform

sources.title: Spline IK
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Setup, chain length, curve target, roll, offset, length/thickness modes, bone-length guidance, hooks
supports: Spline IK aligns connected bones to a curve and is suitable for ropes
Y Scale Mode can stretch to fit, use pre-IK scale, or keep original length
Roughly equal bone lengths and control points every few bones are recommended
Hooks are recommended for curve control points
limits: Length preservation is not universal across scale modes
Constraint evaluation must be baked for non-Blender consumers
No runtime collision or engine guarantee

sources.title: Bendy Bones (B-Bones)
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: B-Bone evaluation, segments, curvature, roll, vertex mapping, keying
supports: B-Bones replace long chains of small rigid bones with a curved bone evaluation
More segments improve smoothness but increase pose cost
Curved vertex mapping costs more than Straight
limits: Not documented as a portable engine runtime feature
No hose/cable-specific material or collision guidance

sources.title: Hook Modifier
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Mesh/curve/lattice hooks, influence, modifier-stack warning, falloff
supports: Hook can control curve control points with another object
Hook stores original indices and should precede generative modifiers
limits: No game-runtime or export guarantee

sources.title: Curve Geometry
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Offset/extrude, taper, bevel depth/resolution/caps, custom profile, tilt
supports: Curves can generate tubes with controlled depth, resolution, and caps
Taper/radius control thickness along length
Custom bevel profiles can create non-circular hose/cable sections
limits: Curve objects are authoring data, not a universal engine asset
No simulation or collision behavior

sources.title: Cloth Introduction
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Modifier behavior/order, apply-to-freeze, cache, CPU cost, workflow, springs, initial penetration
supports: Cloth is a modifier evaluated in stack order
Applying Cloth freezes the current shape and removes the modifier
Simulation results are cached; computation is CPU-intensive
Initial penetration can make simulation unstable
limits: No engine runtime or export guarantee
No direct bag/tent recipe

sources.title: Cloth Examples - Flag and Cloth on Armature
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Flag grid/pin/simulate/apply workflow; cloth on armature pinning; modifier order; bind pose and teleport caveats
supports: A flag can be a grid with its pole edge pinned, simulated, then frozen
Cloth can be pinned to an armature with a vertex group
Cloth modifier is below the Armature modifier in the example stack
Fast movement or teleport can break cloth simulation
limits: Text steps only; no finished flag asset or engine export
No bag/tent/soft-toy example in the read text

sources.title: Cloth Shape - Pin Group, Sewing, Dynamic Mesh
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Pin weights, stiffness, sewing springs/max force, shrinking, dynamic mesh, rest shape key
supports: Pin group vertex weights control how strongly cloth is held
Sewing springs connect two cloth regions and need bounded force for stability
Dynamic Mesh and Rest Shape Key are distinct rest-shape workflows
limits: No universal pin weight or spring value
No engine runtime guarantee

sources.title: Cloth Physical Properties
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Mass, air viscosity, tension/compression/shear/bending, internal springs, pressure, volume, non-manifold caveat
supports: Cloth material behavior is split into tension, compression, shear, and bending
Internal springs can make a mesh behave like a soft body
Pressure can simulate soft-shelled objects but is gas-like, not actual fluid simulation
Non-manifold holes allow pressure to escape and cause drift
limits: No direct bag pattern or seam construction
Pressure is an approximation, not fluid dynamics

sources.title: Cloth Collisions
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Prerequisites, quality, object collision, self collision, distance/impulse, troubleshooting
supports: Collision objects must be meshes with Collision enabled and share layers
Higher quality reduces tears/penetration at more time cost
Self-collision is recommended for close-up cloth but adds compute cost
Increasing stiffness can help cloth torn by a deforming mesh
limits: No engine runtime collision guarantee
No universal quality/distance threshold

sources.title: Cloth Cache
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Baking, cache invalidation after moving/editing, subdivision-level caching, start/end restrictions
supports: Moving/editing cloth after simulation requires clearing the cache
Cache is per subdivision level; render and preview levels should match
Start/end frames cannot change without clearing the bake
limits: No export format or engine cache guarantee
No performance numbers

sources.title: Soft Body Goal and Aerodynamics
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Goal semantics, goal weights, aerodynamic edge force, spring/damping technical model
supports: Goal 1 means no soft-body simulation; goal 0 means full physical influence
Goal can be driven by vertex group weights
Soft-body edges can receive wind/aerodynamic force
limits: No soft-toy or bag-specific asset example
No engine runtime guarantee

sources.title: Soft Body Collision
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Vertex-based collisions, mesh collider requirement, face/edge collision cost, troubleshooting
supports: Soft-body collision is primarily vertex-based; sparse meshes miss collisions
Collision objects must be meshes with Collision enabled
Face collision is expensive and difficult to control
limits: No universal mesh density
No game engine behavior

sources.title: Rigid Body Introduction
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Rigid-body purpose, active/passive, mesh-only, animation interaction, apply-transform note
supports: Rigid body changes position/orientation but does not deform geometry
Only mesh objects can be rigid bodies
Rigid-body simulation interacts with the animation system
limits: No chain-specific setup
No engine runtime guarantee

sources.title: Rigid Body Tips
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Animated passive mistake, bake-to-keyframes, small-object stability, fast-object tunneling, scaling
supports: Animated passive colliders must have the Animated option enabled
Rigid-body dynamics can be baked to normal keyframes
Small/fast objects can tunnel or be unstable; Blender gives a 20 cm example guideline
limits: The 20 cm note is Blender simulation guidance, not a universal asset-size gate
No chain-specific link solution

sources.title: Rigid Body Constraints Introduction
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Joints, empty-hosted constraints, local anchor behavior, limits, breakable, iterations
supports: Rigid-body constraints connect two bodies and are often hosted on an empty
Constraint anchors are fixed in each object's local coordinates for the simulation
Constraints can have limits and be breakable
limits: No chain wrap/friction recipe
No engine runtime guarantee

sources.title: Surface Deform Modifier
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Proxy-driven deformation, binding requirements, global-coordinate binding, falloff, sparse bind
supports: A low-resolution mesh can drive a high-resolution mesh via Surface Deform
Official documentation names cloth simulation proxy as a use case
Binding uses global coordinates; later object transforms are ignored
limits: DCC workflow only; no engine runtime guarantee
Requires well-matching meshes and valid target topology

sources.title: Bake Action
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Bake Action section: final motion, visual keying, clear constraints, frame step, channels
supports: Bake Action computes final motion including constraints/drivers into keys
Visual Keying and Clear Constraints are explicit options
Baking is the route from evaluated rig behavior to explicit animation
limits: Does not make unsupported simulation models portable
No engine import guarantee

sources.title: Shape Keys Introduction
sources.author: Blender Documentation Team / Blender Foundation
sources.read_scope: Relative versus absolute shape keys, morph-target terminology, use cases
supports: Shape keys deform vertices into new shapes and are equivalent to morph targets
Relative keys are for blended shapes; absolute keys are for sequential deformation
limits: Not a continuous collision/physics solution
No runtime support guarantee

sources.title: Cable Components in Unreal Engine
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: Simulation/rendering, plugin activation, placement, Blueprint, end attachment, collision/stiffness, property table
sources.evidence_type: official engine documentation with stepwise operations
supports: Cable simulation uses Verlet particles with distance constraints
Rendering is a separate tube mesh built by a scene proxy
One or both ends can be attached; disabling Attach End makes a free end
Collision and stiffness greatly increase cost; Collision is Experimental
limits: No Blender workflow; no chain-link physical simulation
Documentation version not a project target
No actual cable was created or run

sources.title: UCableComponent API
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: Cable length, segments, solver iterations, substepping, collision, friction, teleport/reattach fields
supports: CableLength is rest length; NumSegments and SolverIterations are explicit controls
Collision is marked Experimental
Teleport/reattach reset fields exist for runtime cable state
limits: No cloth, chain-link, or vegetation behavior
No runtime verification in this research

sources.title: NoxWings/Cable-Component
sources.author: NoxWings (GitHub)
sources.read_scope: CableComponent.cs, CableParticle.cs, README.md, ProjectVersion.txt; repository tree
sources.evidence_type: open-source implementation source; no license file observed
supports: Minimal Verlet particle cable with fixed/free ends
Separate simulation and LineRenderer update
Stiffness solver is an empty TODO; collision is absent
Demonstrates why minimal motion is not production acceptance
limits: No license file observed; do not reuse or redistribute
No collision, no production geometry, no chain/cloth
Code read only; not compiled or run
Unity 5.4.0f3 is an old version

sources.title: Per-Platform LODs
sources.author: Epic Games
sources.read_scope: Ordered LOD sets, reduced geometry and bones, project-dependent severity
supports: Higher LODs can reduce geometry and bone counts
LOD step severity is project-specific
limits: No universal distance or segment-count gate
No flexible-asset-specific guidance
